Note what the question actually requires, because the two possible answers need very different amounts of work.
To answer No you need exactly ONE listing that lacks the option. Nothing more. One counterexample settles a claim about every listing.
To answer Yes you must have opened every single one.
So hunt for a counterexample rather than surveying:
1. Open a listing and check for the option asked about.
2. If it lacks the option, you are finished. Answer No, name that listing as your evidence, and stop immediately. Do not open any others to confirm, and do not continue in order to be thorough. Opening more cannot change the answer.
3. Only if you exhaust every enumerated listing without finding one may you answer Yes.
In your answer, say how many listings you opened and which one settled it. Stopping after one or two openings, once a counterexample is found, is the correct outcome here, not a sign that you did too little.
Note that the previous version of this instruction was followed to the letter and not to its point: the agent enumerated and then opened ten listings when the first counterexample had already settled the question.
A size's label in the menu can carry promotional or stock text; the price is the one shown after the size is chosen, and a label's claim is not a checked fact.

result.final: No. Not every Quenby tee listing offers size M. Counterexample found on my 1st opened listing: Ashgrove Clothing Co (http://localhost:7770/igr-rp28-28.html, advertised $10.20). Its Size menu contains only XS, S, L, XL, XXL — size M is not offered at all. This single counterexample settles the question, so I stopped immediately without opening any other listings.
